analysis.title: UBS Equity Compass: The bar is high (November 2026)
key_insights: UBS CIO downgraded global equities and US equities from Attractive to Neutral. It describes this as a more balanced risk-reward, not a bearish outlook. It advises staying invested but diversified and using strength to rebalance concentrated positions rather than add broad US equity risk.
The ten largest US companies are just shy of 40% of the S&P 500. UBS says this makes index returns sensitive to the results of a small group of companies.
S&P 500 targets: June 2027 cut to 8,000 from 8,400, new December 2027 target of 8,200. Bull case 9,500 and bear case 5,500 for December 2027. Spot is 7,550.

S&P 500 EPS estimates raised to USD 360 for 2026 (+29%) and USD 415 for 2027 (+15%). The increases mainly reflect stronger Q3 results and updated Q4 expectations. Prior estimates were below consensus.

UBS expects US earnings growth, earnings revisions, AI capex growth and ISM Manufacturing to shift from accelerating to decelerating in 2027. It expects more moderate upside and more range-bound trading in 2027.
UBS expects the Fed rate-hiking cycle to end in early 2027. Inflation has to improve for investors to be confident the Fed does not need to move rates into restrictive territory.

US sector changes: financials cut from Attractive to Neutral on slower growth and a less constructive deregulation backdrop. Energy cut from Neutral to Unattractive after strong performance and better prospects for de-escalation in the Middle East.

Eurozone stays Attractive. Eurozone EPS growth forecast raised to 20% in 2026 (from 15%), 15% in 2027, and 8% in 2028. European cyclicals have underperformed defensives by about 17% since mid-June, which UBS says has run ahead of fundamentals.
EuroStoxx 50 June 2027 target trimmed to 6,800 from 7,100 because higher bond yields weigh on valuations. December 2027 target is 7,000, bull 7,700, bear 4,700.

European utilities upgraded to Attractive on data-center and electrification demand and a forward P/E de-rating from 16.8x to 15.3x. European consumer discretionary cut to Neutral because weak Chinese demand for autos and luxury affects about 60% of the sector by market cap.

Switzerland downgraded to Neutral because defensive upside is limited after the rotation. SMI EPS is expected to grow 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027. Targets are 15,300 for June 2027 and 15,500 for December 2027. UBS tactically prefers Swiss mid-caps and quality cyclicals.

Japan, Emerging Markets, Taiwan and Asia ex-Japan moved from Attractive to Neutral. Australia was also downgraded to Neutral. The reasons are AI capex uncertainty in 2028, tighter regulation of AI data centers and financing constraints.

Asia ex-Japan EPS growth forecast is 72% in 2026 and 20% in 2027. Asia ex-Japan and EM trade at 8.3x forward earnings. UBS keeps China A-shares over H-shares, helped by government-backed ETF purchases since October. India stays Attractive. Indonesia stays Unattractive.

AI capex forecast raised to USD 1.0tr in 2026 (from 900bn), USD 1.4tr in 2027 (from 1.2tr), with a new USD 1.5tr forecast for 2028. UBS says the key uncertainty is 2028, and it sees rising risk of a mid-cycle capex digestion over the next 12 months.

Alphabet and Meta reported Q3 2026 free cash flow of about negative USD 9bn and negative USD 1bn respectively. UBS says the relevant question is whether the capital earns an adequate return. US hyperscalers and frontier labs have more than USD 4.2tr of future spending commitments.
UBS estimates AI revenue run rate at under USD 200bn. AI model revenues would need to approach a couple of trillion dollars toward the end of the decade to justify the investment.
The Nasdaq 100 fell by high single digits over the past month despite resilient hyperscaler Q3 results.

In AI, UBS prefers large hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet) over semiconductor and hardware names. Within semis it prefers compute (NVIDIA, Broadcom, AMD), then foundry (TSMC), then equipment (ASML, Applied Materials). It sees memory, optics and substrates as more vulnerable if 2028 capex is revised down.

US midterm results (Democrats took both chambers and flipped governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas) raise data-center delay and cost risk. Newly Democratic governors influence about 40% of planned data-center capacity, with Texas and Georgia about 30%.

Power and resources TRIO stays Attractive with high conviction. UBS says the post-election sell-off improved risk-reward. It models 90 GW of US data-center build by 2030 against about 400 GW of proposals, and equipment backlogs carry onerous cancellation terms.

Longevity TRIO stays Attractive but selective. The MSCI ACWI Health Care index is at a record, up 14% YTD. Lilly reported 39% revenue growth on GLP-1s and materially raised its full-year outlook. Medtech lags and valuations are above historical averages.

Quant: momentum factor has lost further as leadership rotated, and Low Risk had its strongest month of the year in October. All four core factors are positive YTD. The CIO multifactor strategy crowding score is below 10.

From 1 November 2026 UBS CIO no longer rates equities as Most Preferred, Bellwether or Least Preferred, and uses a 'CIO Selected' designation instead. Selected stocks are drawn from those covered by IB Global Research and rated Buy or Neutral.

earnings_insights: UBS raised its S&P 500 EPS estimates to USD 360 for 2026 (+29%) and USD 415 for 2027 (+15%), mainly on stronger Q3 results and updated Q4 expectations. These are the bank's estimates, not company prints.
Eli Lilly reported Q3 2026 revenue growth of 39%, mostly from its GLP-1 franchise, and materially raised its full-year outlook (UBS commentary, no EPS figure given).
Alphabet and Meta reported Q3 2026 free cash flow of about negative USD 9bn and negative USD 1bn respectively. These are reported figures.
UBS forecasts Eurozone earnings growth of 20% in 2026, 15% in 2027 and 8% in 2028 (forecast).

UBS forecasts SMI earnings growth of 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027, UK FTSE 100 EPS growth of 24% in 2026 and 6% in 2027, MSCI Asia ex-Japan EPS growth of 72% in 2026 and 20% in 2027, and Japan TOPIX EPS growth of 12% and 10% (fiscal years ending March 2027 and March 2028). All are forecasts.
Q3 results in Europe show accelerating revenue growth, recovering margins and unusually positive earnings revisions. Q3 results in Switzerland show improving and broadening sales and profit.
Q4 2026 earnings season is expected in Jan-Feb 2027, and European full-year results in Feb-Mar 2027.

Spending keeps rising but growth slows sharply in 2028, which is the main uncertainty.

trade_ideas.description: Long large hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet) over semiconductor and hardware companies
trade_ideas.rationale: Constraints on data-center supply raise the value of existing capacity, and if 2028 capex expectations fall, hyperscaler free cash flow should improve.
trade_ideas.risk: Negative FCF in Q3 for Alphabet and Meta, and capex-return concerns.

trade_ideas.description: Within semiconductors, prefer compute (NVIDIA, Broadcom, AMD), then foundry (TSMC), then equipment (ASML, Applied Materials)
trade_ideas.rationale: Returns supported by high barriers to entry and technological leadership rather than scarcity-driven price increases.

trade_ideas.description: Use market strength to rebalance concentrated US megacap positions rather than add broad US equity risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Top ten companies are just shy of 40% of the index, and returns are sensitive to a small group.

trade_ideas.description: Favor European equities over the US, UK and Switzerland, plus European utilities and health care as portfolio ballast
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings growth is accelerating, revisions are positive, and the sell-off ran ahead of fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker AI demand, a broader slowdown or second-round inflation effects.

trade_ideas.rationale: Government-backed purchases and stabilization set a floor, with better earnings momentum and semiconductor and technology exposure.
trade_ideas.risk: Weak overseas demand and external market volatility.

risk_factors: Slower AI monetization or a mid-cycle capex digestion in 2028, with more selective financing.
Power generation, grid connectivity, equipment availability and permitting constraints on data-center build-out. US midterms add the risk of local moratoria and higher costs.
Market concentration and crowded AI positioning.
Persistently higher bond yields weighing on valuations, and inflation that stays too high for the Fed to stop hiking.
Weaker AI demand, a broader European slowdown or second-round inflation effects in Europe.
Policy and drug-pricing scrutiny for US health care ahead of the 2028 election.
Middle East re-escalation and higher oil prices.
AI disruption of incumbents' businesses and profit pools.
charts_described: Global AI capex chart shows USD 1,021bn in 2026E, USD 1,405bn in 2027E and USD 1,520bn in 2028E, with growth of 109% in 2026E, 38% in 2027E and 8% in 2028E.
European cyclicals vs defensives chart highlights previous major pullbacks of -23%, -22%, -16% and -11%, against the current -17%.
Valuation chart shows 12-month forward P/E, including USA at 18.5x, MSCI AC World at 18.6x, Eurozone at 14.3x and Emerging Markets at 8.4x.
China ETF chart compares the share of ETF flows into STAR, ChiNext and CSI 300 across three periods, including 13-23 October 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Technology stocks have been volatile. The Nasdaq 100 fell by high single digits over the past month.
Factor rotation: momentum lost further as leadership shifted, and Low Risk had its strongest month of the year in October. Quality was positive and Value was broadly flat.

The CIO multifactor quant strategy has a crowding score below 10, on a scale from -30 (extreme short crowding) to +30 (extreme long crowding). It is slightly above pre-Covid levels and has been low and stable through 2026.
UBS flags crowded positioning in the AI trade as a risk because an unwind can amplify price moves and volatility.
The ten largest US companies are just shy of 40% of the S&P 500.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on 3 November produced a Democratic majority in both chambers and flipped governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas, creating divided government for the final two years of the Trump administration.

The Iran war began in February. UBS cites increased prospects for resolution or de-escalation of the Iran crisis and the Middle East conflict as a reason for lower oil prices and a downgrade of US energy.
Potential Russia-Ukraine peace progress is listed as a 2027 catalyst for Europe.
French presidential election on 18 April 2027 with a run-off on 2 May 2027, and German state elections in April-May 2027.
US-China tensions and US export controls appear in company risk factors. Tighter regulation of AI data centers is cited as a risk to Japan's AI capex outlook.
MSCI's reclassification of the MSCI Indonesia index is an overhang for Indonesian equities.
The Brazil election result is cited as pressuring Brazil's domestic market.
cross_bank_references: UBS Global Research (the Investment Bank) is the source for the CIO Selected universe: stocks covered by IB Global Research and rated Buy or Neutral.
Chart source note cites MS Research for China ETF flow data.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler cloud growth is robust, backlogs are expanding, and AI capex forecasts were raised to USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. S&P 500 EPS estimates are USD 360 and USD 415, and the targets of 8,000 and 8,200 still imply upside.
tension_points.bear_case: AI revenue run rate is under USD 200bn against a couple of trillion needed by the end of the decade. Alphabet and Meta free cash flow was negative in Q3, and financing may become more selective. Concentration leaves the index sensitive to a few names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Downward revisions to 2028 AI capex, or monetization that fails to ramp quickly enough, would undermine the bull case. The bear case is USD 5,500 on the S&P 500 by December 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Committed capital, onerous cancellation terms on transformer, switchgear and turbine backlogs, and flexible hyperscalers mean delays extend rather than end the cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic governors influence about 40% of planned capacity, and Texas's incoming governor campaigned on pausing approvals and ending tax abatements. Ohio municipalities have moratoria on ballots.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Actual pauses in data-center approvals, tax abatement removal or local moratoria in Texas, Georgia or Ohio would weaken the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue growth is accelerating, margins are recovering, revisions are positive, and Eurozone EPS growth is 20% in 2026 and 15% in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher bond yields weigh on valuations and led UBS to cut the June 2027 EuroStoxx 50 target to 6,800. Weaker AI demand or second-round inflation effects are risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker AI demand, a broader economic slowdown or second-round inflation effects, though UBS says it sees limited evidence of these so far.

theme_stances.evidence: the investment case is becoming more selective

theme_stances.key_argument: The sell-off has run ahead of fundamentals, with accelerating revenue growth, recovering margins and positive revisions.
theme_stances.evidence: the sell-off has run ahead of any deterioration in fundamentals
